title: Measuring CPT-1-mediated respiration in permeabilized cells and isolated mitochondria
protocol: Warm 1× MAS medium in a 37°C water bath.
Prepare injectates by adding stock concentrations of mitochondrial effectors made in 95% (v/v) EtOH to plain 1× MAS medium without BSA.
Vortex the mixture to ensure thorough mixing.
Pipette 25 μL of each injectate solution into the corresponding port(s).
Use a multichannel pipette with the manufacturer-provided loading guides if desired.
Pipette gently but confidently.
Ensure liquid makes a full seal covering the opening of the port.
Familiarize with the dilutions and concentrations required for sequential injections.
Warm the utility plate in a non-CO2, 37°C benchtop incubator.
Warm the cartridge in a non-CO2, 37°C benchtop incubator.
Design the plate map on the Seahorse controller’s Wave application.
Define the injections, pre-treatments, assay medium, and cell/mitochondria types.
Label each well with the respective conditions.
Define background wells for outer wells used during cell culture.
Mix permeabilized cells for 1 minute and 30 seconds.
Wait for 0 minutes.
Measure permeabilized cells for 2 minutes and 30 seconds.
Mix isolated mitochondria for 1 minute and 30 seconds.
Wait for 0 minutes.
Measure isolated mitochondria for 2 minutes.
Remove the lid from the cartridge before starting calibration.
Place the cartridge and utility plate in the thermal tray with letters right-side up, aligned on the left of the plate.
Prepare the assay medium for permeabilized cells.
Include 1× MAS supplemented with ADP, BSA, and permeabilization reagent (rPFO) in the assay medium for permeabilized cells.
Add appropriate oxidizable substrates to the assay medium for permeabilized cells.
Prepare 2 mL of assay medium for each experimental group to account for dead volume in the pipette or spills.
Wash the Seahorse XF cell plate with unsupplemented 1× MAS medium.
Remove remaining medium from the inner 60 wells using a multichannel pipette, leaving roughly 20 μL per well.
Add 130 μL of 1× MAS medium to each well after removing most of the previous medium.
Repeat washing process two more times for each well.
Avoid touching the bottom of the well with pipet tips during the washing process.
Use an aspirator or multichannel pipette to completely remove medium from background wells around the rim.
Replace removed medium in background wells with 150 μL of unsupplemented MAS.
Remove all but about 20 μL of medium from the plate, including background wells.
Add 130 μL of assay medium with substrates to the desired groups and background wells.
Warm the plate in a benchtop non-CO2 incubator set to 37°C for 5 minutes.
Replace the ejected utility plate with the cell plate after removing the lid when calibration is complete.
Verify that the instrument is running properly before leaving it.
Prepare the assay medium with 1× MAS supplemented with ADP, BSA, and appropriate oxidizable substrates.
Budget for 1 mL of assay medium for every 5 experimental wells.
Chill on ice a total of 3 mL of MAS supplemented with ADP and BSA per plate.
Place a Seahorse XF plate on ice.
Dilute mitochondria to the appropriate concentration per well using the chilled medium from step 4.
Add 7.5 μL of mitochondrial stock to 3 mL of medium to achieve a final concentration of 0.15 mg/mL.
Add 20 μL of diluted mitochondria solution to each experimental well for a final yield of 3 μg/well.
Determine the protein concentration for mouse liver mitochondria using the BCA protein assay.
Gently mix the diluted mitochondrial solution by pipetting up and down.
Empty contents of the tube into the chilled basin (on ice).
Plate 20 μl of the mitochondrial solution into each well in a chilled Seahorse plate.
Leave four wells as background wells, filling these with 20 μl of plain medium.
Centrifuge the plate for 20 min at 2000 g without acceleration or brake.
Adjust instrument settings to avoid disturbing the mitochondrial layer during centrifugation.
Return the plate to ice after centrifugation.
Add 130 μl of assay medium with substrates to the desired groups and background wells.
Add assay medium to the background wells.
Warm the plate in a benchtop non-CO2 incubator set to 37°C for 5 minutes.
Remove the lid from the cell plate before inserting it into the instrument after calibration is complete.
Ensure the instrument is running properly and do not leave until verification is done.
Fix permeabilized cells by adding 25 μL of 16% (v/v) paraformaldehyde to each well in a chemical fume hood.
Add 100 μL of PBS to each well, ensuring a final volume of 200 μL.
Let the plate rest for at least 30 minutes after adding the solution.
Avoid touching the bottom of the wells with pipette tips and be gentle when aspirating to prevent disruption of the cell monolayer.
Seal the edges of the plate with parafilm.
Store the sealed plate at 4°C for several days until further use.
Make 7 mL of a 20 μg/μL Hoechst 33342 solution in PBS per plate.
Mix the Hoechst 33342 solution thoroughly.
Remove 100 μL of medium from the inner wells of the plate.
Add 100 μL of the Hoechst 33342 solution to each well for a final concentration of 10 μg/μL in 2% (w/v) paraformaldehyde.
Wrap the plate in aluminum foil.
Let the plate sit at least 30 minutes at 21°C or for 8-48 hours at 4°C.
Count the number of nuclei per plate using a high content imaging system.
Blacket out the three risers in the Seahorse XF well to avoid complications with automated cell counting.

Normalize oxygen consumption rates from permeabilized Seahorse XF data to pmol O2/min/1 × 103 cells using the normalization tab in the Seahorse XF Wave software or after the assay is completed in spreadsheet software.
